notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 is null (not scored) for those axes. A5/A7/G1/G3/G6/G7 graded on all 3 runs. Board (visualize_board.sh 3333311115554535522024412246261666006): only columns 1 and 5 are open (heights 3 and 4); opponent P1 holds two top-row winning squares, c1r6 and c5r6, neither gravity-top; solver scr = col1 0 (draw), col5 -2 (loss). Playing column 5 lands c5r5 and makes c5r6 gravity-top, so P1 wins at once — every run names exactly that cause, matching lostResource.completingCell=c5r6, window c4r6-c7r6 and opponentPunishment.tag=immediate_threat. All three runs emit the full requiredSet (opp-major-2, opp-key-line, better-col) except run 1, which wraps c5r6 and col1 but names the top-row four-line in plain prose ("su linea de cuatro en la fila de arriba") rather than the opp-key-line handle; mechanical G7a/G7b membership passed for all runs and A7b referents stay locatable in prose, so this is not charged. annotationRepairs empty and guardDiagnostics.failures/strippedSpecs empty on all 3 runs. A5 Spanish voice is correct product voice: 2nd-person voseo ("le dejaste", "vos ya no podes"), no internal-vocabulary echo; "ese recurso" in runs 0/2 reads as ordinary Spanish tactical vocabulary ("that resource/option"), not an echo of the lostResource field name, and is not charged. HARNESS ARTIFACT, not a model or production defect: runs 0 and 2 serve the English fragment "column 5, row 6" inside Spanish prose because compute.mjs computeServedExplanation (connect-four/server/scripts/compute.mjs:341-348) calls guardExplainMoveLlmPayload WITHOUT a locale argument, so humanizeGroundedCoordinates falls back to locale=en; the guard is locale-aware (reasonRenderGuard.mjs:156-159 serverT(locale,"cell") yields "columna c, fila r") and production threads req.locale at index.js:1470, so a real es player would read "columna 5, fila 6". Per the v2 addendum this rewrite is explicitly not an A5 charge; flagged here for the harness owner. Minor, uncharged: run 2 has a gender-agreement slip ("un amenaza" should be "una amenaza"). Missed teaching opportunity (uncharged): the projectedDeep board was shown and encodes the real lesson - by filling column 1 (3 empty, odd) first you end up occupying BOTH c1r6 and c5r6 - but no run explains that parity/occupation idea; all three settle for "column 1 cut that entry and kept the draw", which is true per lostResource.kind=denial/verdict=occupation (P2 takes c5r6 at ply 42 of lostResource.finalMovestring) but thin.
